Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

10	MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1 << 20  # 1 MiB cap on request bodies
11	
12	# Token-gated checkpoint-history routes. Every request to one of these is
13	# rejected before the body is read or any state is touched unless the node was
14	# started with --history* and the request authenticates: the configured static
15	# bearer token is full-power, or the active persisted credential presents a
16	# token hash covering the route's permission. POST /v1/history/access manages
17	# that credential and is reserved for the static token.
18	HISTORY_ROUTES = {
19	    ("GET", "/v1/history/trust"),
20	    ("POST", "/v1/history/trust"),
21	    ("POST", "/v1/history/export"),
22	    ("POST", "/v1/history/access"),
23	}
24	
25	
26	def build_handler(service: LedgerService) -> type[BaseHTTPRequestHandler]:
27	    """Create a handler class closed over the given ledger service."""
28	
29	    class LedgerHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
30	        server_version = "VerifiableLedger/1.0"
31	
32	        # -- helpers --------------------------------------------------------
33	
34	        def _send_json(
35	            self, status: int, body: dict, sort_keys: bool = True
36	        ) -> None:
37	            data = json.dumps(
38	                body, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=sort_keys
39	            ).encode("utf-8")
40	            self.send_response(status)
41	            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
42	            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
43	            self.end_headers()
44	            self.wfile.write(data)
45	
46	        def _history_authorized(self, method: str, path: str) -> bool:
47	            """Bearer-token gate for the /v1/history/* routes.
48	
49	            Returns True when the request may proceed. When the feature is
50	            disabled the gate is open (the service answers 404); otherwise the
51	            request is authenticated before the body is read or any state is
52	            touched. The configured static token is full-power; an active
53	            persisted credential whose token hash matches is admitted only for
54	            routes covered by its permission set. A missing/malformed/unknown
55	            bearer is answered 401 (``unauthorized``); an authenticated
56	            credential lacking the route's permission is answered 403
57	            (``forbidden``). Both failures happen without reading the body,
58	            appending an audit event or touching any file.
59	            """
60	            if (method, path) not in HISTORY_ROUTES:
61	                return True
62	            if not getattr(service, "history_enabled", False):
63	                return True
64	            required = service.history_route_permission(method, path)
65	            provided = self.headers.get("Authorization")
66	            outcome = service.authorize_history(provided, required)
67	            if outcome == "ok":
68	                return True
69	            error = "unauthorized" if outcome == "unauthorized" else "forbidden"
70	            self._send_json(
71	                401 if error == "unauthorized" else 403,
72	                {"ok": False, "error": error},
73	                sort_keys=False,
74	            )
75	            # The body was deliberately not consumed: close the connection so
76	            # an unread Content-Length body cannot desync the next pipelined
77	            # request on a keep-alive socket.
78	            self.close_connection = True
79	            return False
80	
81	
82	        def _read_json(self) -> tuple[bool, object]:
83	            try:
84	                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
85	            except ValueError:
86	                return False, {"error": "invalid Content-Length"}
87	            if length <= 0:
88	                return False, {"error": "request body must be JSON"}
89	            if length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
90	                return False, {"error": "request body too large"}
91	            raw = self.rfile.read(length)
92	            try:
93	                return True, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
94	            except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
95	                return False, {"error": "request body must be valid JSON"}

"""HTTP server exposing the ledger REST API using the Python standard library."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, unquote

from .service import LedgerService

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1 << 20  # 1 MiB cap on request bodies

# Token-gated checkpoint-history routes. Every request to one of these is
# rejected before the body is read or any state is touched unless the node was
# started with --history* and the request authenticates: the configured static
# bearer token is full-power, or the active persisted credential presents a
# token hash covering the route's permission. POST /v1/history/access manages
# that credential and is reserved for the static token.
HISTORY_ROUTES = {
    ("GET", "/v1/history/trust"),
    ("POST", "/v1/history/trust"),
    ("POST", "/v1/history/export"),
    ("POST", "/v1/history/access"),
}


def build_handler(service: LedgerService) -> type[BaseHTTPRequestHandler]:
    """Create a handler class closed over the given ledger service."""

    class LedgerHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        server_version = "VerifiableLedger/1.0"

        # -- helpers --------------------------------------------------------

        def _send_json(
            self, status: int, body: dict, sort_keys: bool = True
        ) -> None:
            data = json.dumps(
                body, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=sort_keys
            ).encode("utf-8")
            self.send_response(status)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(data)

        def _history_authorized(self, method: str, path: str) -> bool:
            """Bearer-token gate for the /v1/history/* routes.

            Returns True when the request may proceed. When the feature is
            disabled the gate is open (the service answers 404); otherwise the
            request is authenticated before the body is read or any state is
            touched. The configured static token is full-power; an active
            persisted credential whose token hash matches is admitted only for
            routes covered by its permission set. A missing/malformed/unknown
            bearer is answered 401 (``unauthorized``); an authenticated
            credential lacking the route's permission is answered 403
            (``forbidden``). Both failures happen without reading the body,
            appending an audit event or touching any file.
            """
            if (method, path) not in HISTORY_ROUTES:
                return True
            if not getattr(service, "history_enabled", False):
                return True
            required = service.history_route_permission(method, path)
            provided = self.headers.get("Authorization")
            outcome = service.authorize_history(provided, required)
            if outcome == "ok":
                return True
            error = "unauthorized" if outcome == "unauthorized" else "forbidden"
            self._send_json(
                401 if error == "unauthorized" else 403,
                {"ok": False, "error": error},
                sort_keys=False,
            )
            # The body was deliberately not consumed: close the connection so
            # an unread Content-Length body cannot desync the next pipelined
            # request on a keep-alive socket.
            self.close_connection = True
            return False


        def _read_json(self) -> tuple[bool, object]:
            try:
                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
            except ValueError:
                return False, {"error": "invalid Content-Length"}
            if length <= 0:
                return False, {"error": "request body must be JSON"}
            if length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
                return False, {"error": "request body too large"}
            raw = self.rfile.read(length)
            try:
                return True, json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
            except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                return False, {"error": "request body must be valid JSON"}

        # -- routing --------------------------------------------------------

        def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 (stdlib naming)
            path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0]
            # Bearer gate first: a 401 must be returned before the body is
            # read and without any state or file side effects.
            if not self._history_authorized("POST", path):
                return
            if path == "/v1/history/access":
                # POST /v1/history/access — rotate/revoke the persistent
                # permissioned credential. Reserved for the static full-power
                # token by the gate above; the success body has the contract
                # key order version, token_hash, permissions, status.
                ok, payload = self._read_json()
                if not ok:
                    self._send_json(
                        400, {"ok": False, "error": "input"}, sort_keys=False
                    )
                    return

    return LedgerHandler


def serve(service: LedgerService, host: str, port: int) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
    """Create and run the HTTP server (blocks until interrupted)."""
    httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), build_handler(service))
    httpd.serve_forever()
    return httpd

16	fixed endowment (``initial_balance``, overridable via LEDGER_INITIAL_BALANCE).
17	An account's confirmed balance is::
18	
19	    initial_balance + sum(confirmed amounts received) - sum(confirmed amounts sent)
20	
21	Only confirmed blocks count. The reported balance additionally subtracts the
22	account's spends sitting in the pending (unconfirmed) tip block — pending
23	*credits* are deliberately not counted. An identity only becomes a *queryable
24	account* once it appears in a confirmed block; GET account before that

140	    def submit_transaction(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
141	        """Validate and enqueue a transaction. Returns (status, body)."""
142	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
143	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
144	        for field in REQUIRED_TX_FIELDS:
145	            if field not in payload:
146	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
147	
148	        sender = payload["from"]
149	        recipient = payload["to"]
150	        amount = payload["amount"]
151	        signature = payload["signature"]
152	
153	        if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
154	            return 400, {"error": "field 'from' must be a non-empty string"}
155	        if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
156	            return 400, {"error": "field 'to' must be a non-empty string"}
157	        # bool is a subclass of int: reject it and all non-int types explicitly.
158	        if not isinstance(amount, int) or isinstance(amount, bool) or amount <= 0:
159	            return 400, {"error": "field 'amount' must be a positive integer"}
160	        if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
161	            return 400, {"error": "field 'signature' must be a non-empty string"}
162	
163	        message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
164	        if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
165	            return 400, {"error": "invalid signature"}
166	
167	        tx = Transaction(sender, recipient, amount, signature)
168	        with self.store.lock:
169	            if tx.tx_id in self.store.pending:
170	                return 409, {"error": "transaction already pending", "tx_id": tx.tx_id}
171	            if any(tx.tx_id == existing.tx_id for block in self.store.chain for existing in block.transactions):
172	                return 409, {"error": "transaction already confirmed", "tx_id": tx.tx_id}
173	            if self.available_balance(sender) < amount:
174	                return 400, {"error": "insufficient balance"}
175	            self.store.pending[tx.tx_id] = tx
176	            try:
177	                self.store.save()
178	            except BaseException:
179	                # Persistence failed: drop the in-memory enqueue so memory
180	                # keeps matching the last durably committed state.
181	                self.store.pending.pop(tx.tx_id, None)
182	                raise
183	        return 202, {"tx_id": tx.tx_id}

185	    def get_transaction(self, tx_id: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
186	        """GET /v1/transactions/{tx_id} — one transaction receipt.
187	
188	        The lookup covers the canonical chain and the mempool only; candidate
189	        forks are never exposed. A ``tx_id`` that is not exactly 64 lowercase
190	        hex characters, or one nothing holds, returns 404.
191	
192	        A mempool transaction is reported ``pending`` with ``height``,
193	        ``block_hash`` and ``index`` all null. A transaction packed into the
194	        unconfirmed tip block is ``pending`` too, anchored at that block with
195	        its 0-based in-block index. A transaction in a confirmed block is
196	        ``confirmed``. Every receipt is built from the stored signed
197	        transaction: the id is recomputed from its canonical message (never
198	        taken from an index or a fork-side cache) and the fields are strictly
199	        re-typed (non-empty strings, a positive non-boolean integer amount),
200	        so adoption, rollback and restart can only ever surface the current
201	        canonical/pending state.
202	        """
203	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id):
204	            return 404, {"error": "transaction not found"}
205	        with self.store.lock:
206	            # Canonical chain first: confirmed blocks, then at most one
207	            # pending tip. The stored signed transaction is the sole source
208	            # for the receipt, and its id is recomputed rather than trusted
209	            # from any lookup key.
210	            for block in self.store.chain:
211	                for index, tx in enumerate(block.transactions):
212	                    if tx.tx_id != tx_id:
213	                        continue
214	                    if not self._is_receipt_tx_well_typed(tx):
215	                        return 404, {"error": "transaction not found"}
216	                    status = (
217	                        STATUS_CONFIRMED
218	                        if block.status == STATUS_CONFIRMED
219	                        else STATUS_PENDING
220	                    )
221	                    return 200, self._transaction_receipt(
222	                        tx, status, block.height, block.block_hash, index
223	                    )
224	            # Still unpacked in the mempool.
225	            tx = self.store.pending.get(tx_id)
226	            if tx is not None:
227	                if not self._is_receipt_tx_well_typed(tx):
228	                    return 404, {"error": "transaction not found"}
229	                return 200, self._transaction_receipt(
230	                    tx, STATUS_PENDING, None, None, None
231	                )
232	            return 404, {"error": "transaction not found"}
233	
234	    @staticmethod
235	    def _is_receipt_tx_well_typed(tx: Transaction) -> bool:
236	        """Strict receipt-time type check of a stored signed transaction.
237	
238	        Every stored transaction already passed these checks at submission
239	        (and again during snapshot recovery); the re-check guarantees a
240	        receipt can never serialize a value that violates the response
241	        contract, even if an in-memory invariant were broken.
242	        """
243	        return (
244	            isinstance(tx.sender, str)
245	            and bool(tx.sender)
246	            and isinstance(tx.recipient, str)
247	            and bool(tx.recipient)
248	            and isinstance(tx.amount, int)
249	            and not isinstance(tx.amount, bool)
250	            and tx.amount > 0
251	            and isinstance(tx.signature, str)
252	            and bool(tx.signature)
253	        )

256	    def _transaction_receipt(
257	        tx: Transaction,
258	        status: str,
259	        height: int | None,
260	        block_hash: str | None,
261	        index: int | None,
262	    ) -> dict:
263	        """The fixed nine-field receipt shape."""
264	        return {
265	            "tx_id": tx.tx_id,
266	            "from": tx.sender,
267	            "to": tx.recipient,
268	            "amount": tx.amount,
269	            "signature": tx.signature,
270	            "status": status,
271	            "height": height,
272	            "block_hash": block_hash,
273	            "index": index,
274	        }

276	    def get_finalized_receipt(self, tx_id: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
277	        """GET /v1/transactions/{tx_id}/finalized-receipt — an offline-verifiable
278	        finalized transaction receipt.
279	
280	        Lookup and typing rules mirror :meth:`get_transaction`: a ``tx_id``
281	        that is not exactly 64 lowercase hex characters, or one nothing
282	        holds on the canonical chain (the mempool and candidate forks are
283	        not matches here), returns 404. A transaction still in the mempool
284	        or packed into the unconfirmed pending tip is not final and returns
285	        409.
286	
287	        On success the whole document is snapshotted under one store lock
288	        together with the current audit signer, so the receipt, proof,
289	        headers and finality credential can never mix chain states. The
290	        body has the fixed key order ``receipt, proof, headers, finality``:
291	        ``receipt`` is the fixed nine-field receipt with ``status``
292	        confirmed; ``proof`` is the single-transaction Merkle proof of
293	        ``GET /v1/blocks/{height}/proof/{tx_id}``; ``headers`` run from the
294	        transaction's own confirmed block up to and including the highest
295	        confirmed block in ascending height, each item in the signed header
296	        page's five-field shape (every item confirmed); and ``finality`` is
297	        exactly the ``GET /v1/chain/finality`` document, whose
298	        ``finalized`` names that last header.
299	        """
300	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id):
301	            return 404, {"error": "transaction not found"}
302	        from . import light_client
303	
304	        with self.store.lock:
305	            matched: tuple[Block, int, Transaction] | None = None
306	            for block in self.store.chain:
307	                for index, tx in enumerate(block.transactions):
308	                    if tx.tx_id == tx_id:
309	                        matched = (block, index, tx)
310	                        break
311	                if matched is not None:
312	                    break
313	            if matched is None:
314	                # Neither the canonical chain nor (below) the mempool holds
315	                # the id; candidate forks are never exposed.
316	                if tx_id in self.store.pending:
317	                    return 409, {"error": "transaction is not confirmed"}
318	                return 404, {"error": "transaction not found"}
319	            block, index, tx = matched
320	            if not self._is_receipt_tx_well_typed(tx):
321	                return 404, {"error": "transaction not found"}
322	            if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
323	                # A packed-but-unconfirmed transaction can only sit in the
324	                # pending chain tip.
325	                return 409, {"error": "transaction is not confirmed"}
326	
327	            tx_ids = [candidate.tx_id for candidate in block.transactions]
328	            proof = {
329	                "height": block.height,
330	                "tx_id": tx.tx_id,
331	                "index": index,
332	                "merkle_root": block.merkle_root,
333	                "block_hash": block.block_hash,
334	                "siblings": crypto.merkle_proof(tx_ids, index),
335	            }
336	
337	            finalized_block = next(
338	                candidate
339	                for candidate in reversed(self.store.chain)
340	                if candidate.status == STATUS_CONFIRMED
341	            )
342	            # Every block from the transaction's block through the highest
343	            # confirmed block is confirmed: the only pending block the chain
344	            # ever carries is its tip, which the slice stops before.
345	            headers = [
346	                self._header_entry(candidate)
347	                for candidate in self.store.chain[
348	                    block.height : finalized_block.height + 1
349	                ]
350	            ]
351	            finalized = self._anchor_descriptor(finalized_block)
352	            tip = self._fork_summary(self.store.chain)
353	            signer = self.store.audit_signer
354	            if signer is None:
355	                # Every snapshot (including migrated legacy ones) carries a
356	                # current audit signer after recovery; reaching here is a
357	                # programming error rather than a client-visible condition.
358	                raise RuntimeError(
359	                    "no audit signer available for finalized receipt"
360	                )
361	            auth = light_client.sign_finality(
362	                signer["private_key"], signer["version"], finalized, tip
363	            )
364	            if auth is None:
365	                raise RuntimeError("current audit signer key is invalid")
366	            finality = {
367	                "finalized": finalized,
368	                "tip": tip,
369	                "auth": auth,
370	            }
371	            return 200, {
372	                "receipt": self._transaction_receipt(
373	                    tx, STATUS_CONFIRMED, block.height, block.block_hash, index
374	                ),
375	                "proof": proof,
376	                "headers": headers,
377	                "finality": finality,
378	            }

380	    def get_finalized_receipts(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
381	        """POST /v1/transactions/finalized-receipts — a batch of
382	        offline-verifiable finalized receipts sharing one chain snapshot.
383	
384	        The body must be a JSON object containing exactly the ``tx_ids``
385	        key: a non-empty list of distinct 64-lowercase-hex strings (the
386	        same rules as ``POST /v1/blocks/{height}/proofs``). A malformed
387	        body — parse failure, missing/extra keys, a wrong type, an empty
388	        list, duplicates or a wrongly formatted id — is 400 and never
389	        touches state. If every id is well formed but any of them is held
390	        neither on the canonical chain nor in the mempool (candidate forks
391	        are never matches), the answer is 404; otherwise, when nothing is
392	        missing but at least one transaction is still in the mempool or
393	        packed into the unconfirmed pending tip, the answer is 409.
394	
395	        On success the chain and the current audit signer are snapshotted
396	        together under one store lock (exactly as for
397	        :meth:`get_finalized_receipt`), so every item, the shared header
398	        run and the finality credential can never mix chain states. The
399	        body has the fixed key order ``items, headers, finality``:
400	        ``items`` is ordered by ``tx_id`` ascending regardless of the
401	        request order, and each item has the fixed key order
402	        ``receipt, proof`` using the exact single-receipt contract;
403	        ``headers`` is the continuous five-field confirmed header run from
404	        the **lowest** transaction's block up to and including the highest
405	        confirmed block (every item confirmed); ``finality`` is exactly the
406	        ``GET /v1/chain/finality`` document, whose ``finalized`` names the
407	        last header.
408	        """
409	        if not isinstance(payload, dict) or set(payload) != {"tx_ids"}:
410	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object with only 'tx_ids'"}
411	        tx_ids_raw = payload["tx_ids"]
412	        if not isinstance(tx_ids_raw, list) or not tx_ids_raw:
413	            return 400, {"error": "field 'tx_ids' must be a non-empty array"}
414	        if any(not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id) for tx_id in tx_ids_raw):
415	            return 400, {
416	                "error": "every tx_id must be a string of 64 lowercase hex characters"
417	            }
418	        if len(set(tx_ids_raw)) != len(tx_ids_raw):
419	            return 400, {"error": "tx_ids must be distinct"}
420	
421	        from . import light_client
422	
423	        with self.store.lock:
424	            requested = sorted(tx_ids_raw)
425	            requested_set = set(requested)
426	            # One pass over the canonical chain (which includes the pending
427	            # tip) locates every request id at its first inclusion point.
428	            located: dict[str, tuple[Block, int, Transaction]] = {}
429	            for block in self.store.chain:
430	                for index, tx in enumerate(block.transactions):
431	                    if tx.tx_id in requested_set and tx.tx_id not in located:
432	                        located[tx.tx_id] = (block, index, tx)
433	            # A 404 takes precedence over a 409: an id absent from both the
434	            # chain and the mempool does not exist, even if another id of
435	            # the same batch is merely unconfirmed.
436	            unknown = [
437	                tx_id
438	                for tx_id in requested
439	                if tx_id not in located
440	                and tx_id not in self.store.pending
441	            ]
442	            if unknown:
443	                return 404, {"error": "transaction not found"}
444	            for tx_id, (_block, _index, tx) in located.items():
445	                if not self._is_receipt_tx_well_typed(tx):
446	                    return 404, {"error": "transaction not found"}
447	            if any(
448	                tx_id in self.store.pending
449	                or located[tx_id][0].status != STATUS_CONFIRMED
450	                for tx_id in requested
451	            ):
452	                # Packed-but-unconfirmed transactions can only sit in the
453	                # pending chain tip; everything else here is in the mempool.
454	                return 409, {"error": "transaction is not confirmed"}
455	
456	            items = []
457	            lowest_height: int | None = None
458	            for tx_id in requested:
459	                block, index, tx = located[tx_id]
460	                if lowest_height is None or block.height < lowest_height:
461	                    lowest_height = block.height
462	                items.append(
463	                    {
464	                        "receipt": self._transaction_receipt(
465	                            tx,
466	                            STATUS_CONFIRMED,
467	                            block.height,
468	                            block.block_hash,
469	                            index,
470	                        ),
471	                        "proof": {
472	                            "height": block.height,
473	                            "tx_id": tx.tx_id,
474	                            "index": index,
475	                            "merkle_root": block.merkle_root,
476	                            "block_hash": block.block_hash,
477	                            "siblings": crypto.merkle_proof(
478	                                [candidate.tx_id for candidate in block.transactions],
479	                                index,
480	                            ),
481	                        },
482	                    }
483	                )
484	
485	            finalized_block = next(
486	                candidate
487	                for candidate in reversed(self.store.chain)
488	                if candidate.status == STATUS_CONFIRMED
489	            )
490	            # The run spans the lowest transaction block through the highest
491	            # confirmed block; every block in between is confirmed because
492	            # the only pending block the chain ever carries is its tip.
493	            assert lowest_height is not None
494	            headers = [
495	                self._header_entry(candidate)
496	                for candidate in self.store.chain[
497	                    lowest_height : finalized_block.height + 1
498	                ]
499	            ]
500	            finalized = self._anchor_descriptor(finalized_block)
501	            tip = self._fork_summary(self.store.chain)
502	            signer = self.store.audit_signer
503	            if signer is None:
504	                # Every snapshot (including migrated legacy ones) carries a
505	                # current audit signer after recovery; reaching here is a
506	                # programming error rather than a client-visible condition.
507	                raise RuntimeError(
508	                    "no audit signer available for finalized receipts"
509	                )
510	            auth = light_client.sign_finality(
511	                signer["private_key"], signer["version"], finalized, tip
512	            )
513	            if auth is None:
514	                raise RuntimeError("current audit signer key is invalid")
515	            return 200, {
516	                "items": items,
517	                "headers": headers,
518	                "finality": {
519	                    "finalized": finalized,
520	                    "tip": tip,
521	                    "auth": auth,
522	                },
523	            }

525	    def audit_receipt_proofs(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
526	        """POST /v1/transactions/receipt-proofs/audit — offline audit summary
527	        for a batch of ``receipt_proof`` documents.
528	
529	        The body must be a JSON object containing exactly the keys
530	        ``documents, expected_root`` in that order: ``documents`` a
531	        non-empty array whose items are each audited under the
532	        ``receipt_proof`` contract and ``expected_root`` the caller-pinned
533	        64-lowercase-hex Merkle root. A malformed body — parse failure,
534	        missing/extra/out-of-order keys, an empty array or an illegal root
535	        — is 400 with the ordered body ``{"ok": false, "error": "input"}``
536	        and never touches state.
537	
538	        A legal batch is answered 200 with the core
539	        :func:`ledger.light_client.receipt_proofs_audit` result verbatim
540	        (key order ``ok, root, total, succeeded, errors, entries,
541	        digest``). The audit is a pure function of the request body: no
542	        state is read or written, so concurrent requests and restarts
543	        yield identical results.
544	        """
545	        if not isinstance(payload, dict) or tuple(payload.keys()) != (
546	            "documents",
547	            "expected_root",
548	        ):
549	            return 400, {"ok": False, "error": "input"}
550	        documents = payload["documents"]
551	        expected_root = payload["expected_root"]
552	        if not isinstance(documents, list) or not documents:
553	            return 400, {"ok": False, "error": "input"}
554	        if not crypto.is_hex64(expected_root):
555	            return 400, {"ok": False, "error": "input"}
556	        from . import light_client
557	
558	        return 200, light_client.receipt_proofs_audit(documents, expected_root)

562	    def mine_block(self) -> tuple[int, dict]:
563	        """Pack all pending transactions (ascending tx_id) into a pending block.
564	
565	        Only allowed when the chain tip is confirmed; the new block becomes
566	        the pending tip until it is confirmed or rolled back.
567	        """
568	        with self.store.lock:
569	            if self.store.tip_is_pending():
570	                return 409, {"error": "tip block is pending confirmation"}
571	            if not self.store.pending:
572	                return 409, {"error": "no pending transactions"}
573	            ordered = sorted(self.store.pending.values(), key=lambda tx: tx.tx_id)
574	            block = Block.create(
575	                height=self.store.next_height(),
576	                prev_hash=self.store.tip_hash(),
577	                transactions=ordered,
578	                status=STATUS_PENDING,
579	            )
580	            self.store.chain.append(block)
581	            removed = [self.store.pending.pop(tx.tx_id) for tx in ordered]
582	            try:
583	                self.store.save()
584	            except BaseException:
585	                # Undo the in-memory block so nothing un-persisted is visible.
586	                self.store.chain.pop()
587	                self.store.pending.update({tx.tx_id: tx for tx in removed})
588	                raise
589	        return 201, {
590	            "height": block.height,
591	            "block_hash": block.block_hash,
592	            "merkle_root": block.merkle_root,
593	            "status": block.status,
594	        }

617	    def confirm_block(self, height: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
618	        """Confirm a pending tip block.
619	
620	        Only a pending chain tip whose parent is confirmed can be confirmed.
621	        Confirming an already-confirmed block is idempotent (200); every
622	        other case — unknown or malformed height, non-tip pending block —
623	        returns 409.
624	        """
625	        height_int = _parse_height(height)
626	        with self.store.lock:
627	            if height_int is None:
628	                return 409, {"error": "block cannot be confirmed"}
629	            block = self.store.block_at(height_int)
630	            if block is None:
631	                return 409, {"error": "block cannot be confirmed"}
632	            if block.status == STATUS_CONFIRMED:
633	                # Idempotent re-confirm.
634	                return 200, {"height": block.height, "status": STATUS_CONFIRMED}
635	            if block is not self.store.tip():
636	                return 409, {"error": "only the chain tip can be confirmed"}
637	            parent = self.store.chain[-2] if len(self.store.chain) >= 2 else None
638	            if parent is None or parent.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
639	                return 409, {"error": "previous block is not confirmed"}
640	            block.status = STATUS_CONFIRMED
641	            try:
642	                self.store.save()
643	            except BaseException:
644	                block.status = STATUS_PENDING
645	                raise
646	            return 200, {"height": block.height, "status": STATUS_CONFIRMED}

648	    def rollback_block(self, height: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
649	        """Roll back a pending tip block: delete it and restore its transactions.
650	
651	        Unknown or malformed heights (including an already-rolled-back
652	        height) return 404; a confirmed block or a non-tip block returns 409.
653	        """
654	        height_int = _parse_height(height)
655	        if height_int is None:
656	            return 404, {"error": "block not found"}
657	        with self.store.lock:
658	            block = self.store.block_at(height_int)
659	            if block is None:
660	                return 404, {"error": "block not found"}
661	            if block.status == STATUS_CONFIRMED:
662	                return 409, {"error": "confirmed block cannot be rolled back"}
663	            if block is not self.store.tip():
664	                return 409, {"error": "only the chain tip can be rolled back"}
665	            pending_before = set(self.store.pending)
666	            rolled_back = self.store.rollback_tip()
667	            try:
668	                self.store.save()
669	            except BaseException:
670	                # Restore the block and drop only the mempool entries we added.
671	                self.store.chain.append(rolled_back)
672	                for tx_id in list(self.store.pending):
673	                    if tx_id not in pending_before:
674	                        del self.store.pending[tx_id]
675	                raise
676	            return 200, {"height": rolled_back.height, "status": "rolled_back"}

711	    def get_proofs(self, height: object, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
712	        """Return Merkle inclusion proofs for a batch of tx_ids at one height.
713	
714	        POST /v1/blocks/{height}/proofs with ``{"tx_ids": [...]}``. The body
715	        must be a JSON object containing exactly the ``tx_ids`` key: a
716	        non-empty list of distinct 64-lowercase-hex strings. A malformed body
717	        — parse failure, missing/extra keys, a wrong type, an empty list,
718	        duplicates or a wrongly formatted id — is 400 and never touches state.
719	        A malformed/unknown height or any requested transaction absent from
720	        the block is 404; proofs are only issued for confirmed blocks, so a
721	        pending block returns 409.
722	
723	        On success the body carries the block's complete ascending
724	        ``transaction_ids`` (every leaf) plus one
725	        ``{tx_id, index, siblings}`` proof per requested id, the proofs sorted
726	        by tx_id; the sibling paths run leaf-to-root exactly like
727	        :meth:`get_proof`.
728	        """
729	        if not isinstance(payload, dict) or set(payload) != {"tx_ids"}:
730	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object with only 'tx_ids'"}
731	        tx_ids_raw = payload["tx_ids"]
732	        if not isinstance(tx_ids_raw, list) or not tx_ids_raw:
733	            return 400, {"error": "field 'tx_ids' must be a non-empty array"}
734	        if any(not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id) for tx_id in tx_ids_raw):
735	            return 400, {
736	                "error": "every tx_id must be a string of 64 lowercase hex characters"
737	            }
738	        if len(set(tx_ids_raw)) != len(tx_ids_raw):
739	            return 400, {"error": "tx_ids must be distinct"}
740	
741	        height_int = _parse_height(height)
742	        if height_int is None:
743	            return 404, {"error": "block not found"}
744	        with self.store.lock:
745	            block = self.store.block_at(height_int)
746	            if block is None:
747	                return 404, {"error": "block not found"}
748	            if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
749	                return 409, {"error": "block is pending confirmation"}
750	            tx_ids = [tx.tx_id for tx in block.transactions]
751	            present = set(tx_ids)
752	            if any(tx_id not in present for tx_id in tx_ids_raw):
753	                return 404, {"error": "transaction not found"}
754	            requested = sorted(set(tx_ids_raw))
755	            proofs = []
756	            for tx_id in requested:
757	                index = tx_ids.index(tx_id)
758	                proofs.append({
759	                    "tx_id": tx_id,
760	                    "index": index,
761	                    "siblings": crypto.merkle_proof(tx_ids, index),
762	                })
763	            return 200, {
764	                "height": block.height,
765	                "block_hash": block.block_hash,
766	                "merkle_root": block.merkle_root,
767	                "transaction_ids": tx_ids,

786	    def _state_tree(
787	        self, chain: list | None = None
788	    ) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]], list[str], str]:
789	        """Build the confirmed account rows (ascending account), their leaves
790	        and the Merkle root, all from the confirmed chain under the current
791	        endowment. ``chain`` defaults to the whole canonical chain; a confirmed
792	        prefix replays historical state deterministically. Caller must hold the
793	        store lock.
794	        """
795	        if chain is None:
796	            chain = self.store.chain
797	        rows = self.store.account_state_rows(chain, self.initial_balance)
798	        leaves = [
799	            crypto.account_state_leaf(account, balance, transactions)
800	            for account, balance, transactions in rows
801	        ]
802	        return rows, leaves, crypto.account_state_root(leaves)

804	    def get_state_root(self, height: object = None) -> tuple[int, dict]:
805	        """GET /v1/state/root and GET /v1/state/root/{height}.
806	
807	        Without a height the tree is anchored to the highest block. A pending
808	        chain tip anchors nothing yet, so the endpoint returns 404 until the
809	        tip is confirmed.
810	
811	        With a path height the state is replayed only from genesis through
812	        that block: the height must be an unsigned decimal without leading
813	        zeros (malformed heights are treated like any unknown path), the block
814	        must exist on the canonical chain and be confirmed — an unknown,
815	        non-canonical or pending height returns 404. The success body has
816	        exactly the same four fields as the unanchored endpoint.
817	        """
818	        with self.store.lock:
819	            if height is None:
820	                anchor = self.store.tip()
821	            else:
822	                # Strict unsigned decimal with no leading zeros, signs or
823	                # whitespace; every malformed value is an unknown path (404).
824	                height_int = _parse_decimal(height)
825	                if height_int is None:
826	                    return 404, {"error": "block not found"}
827	                anchor = self.store.block_at(height_int)
828	                if anchor is None:
829	                    return 404, {"error": "block not found"}
830	            if anchor.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
831	                return 404, {"error": "chain tip is pending confirmation"}
832	            prefix = self.store.chain if height is None else self.store.chain[: anchor.height + 1]
833	            rows, _leaves, root = self._state_tree(prefix)
834	            return 200, {
835	                "state_root": root,
836	                "height": anchor.height,
837	                "block_hash": anchor.block_hash,
838	                "account_count": len(rows),
839	            }

845	        account-state tree.
846	
847	        Without ``height`` the proof is anchored to the highest (confirmed)
848	        block. With ``height=H`` the state is deterministically replayed from
849	        the canonical confirmed prefix through that block only: the value must
850	        be a plain non-negative decimal without leading zeros (a malformed or
851	        repeated query parameter is 400), and an unknown/non-canonical/pending
852	        anchor height is 404. ``height`` is the only accepted query parameter;
853	        any unknown parameter is 400. Returns 404 while a pending tip anchors
854	        the default view, or for an account absent from the (historical)
855	        confirmed account set.

859	            if any(key != "height" for key in params):
860	                return 400, {"error": "unknown query parameter"}
861	            height_raw = params.get("height")
862	        anchor_height: int | None = None
863	        if height_raw is not None:

930	        anchor_height: int | None = None
931	        if height_raw is not None:
932	            anchor_height = _parse_decimal(height_raw)
933	            if anchor_height is None:
934	                return 400, {"error": "height must be a non-negative decimal"}
935	        from . import light_client

937	        with self.store.lock:

940	            else:

952	            index = next(

954	                None,
955	            )
956	            if index is None:

958	            account_name, balance, transactions = rows[index]
959	            siblings = crypto.merkle_proof(leaves, index)
960	            state = {

1000	    def reported_balance(self, account: str) -> int:
1001	        """Confirmed balance minus spends sitting in the pending tip block.
1002	
1003	        Pending-block credits are not counted: unconfirmed income can still
1004	        be rolled back, so it must not inflate the reported balance.
1005	        """
1006	        balance = self.confirmed_balance(account)
1007	        tip = self.store.tip()
1008	        if tip.status == STATUS_PENDING:
1009	            for tx in tip.transactions:
1010	                if tx.sender == account:
1011	                    balance -= tx.amount
1012	        return balance

1014	    def available_balance(self, account: str) -> int:
1015	        """Reported balance minus amounts already committed in the mempool.
1016	
1017	        Pending credits (mempool or unconfirmed block) are deliberately not
1018	        counted, so a sequence of submissions cannot spend money that has not
1019	        been confirmed yet.
1020	        """
1021	        balance = self.reported_balance(account)
1022	        for tx in self.store.pending.values():
1023	            if tx.sender == account:
1024	                balance -= tx.amount
1025	        return balance

1029	    @staticmethod
1030	    def _fork_summary(blocks: list) -> dict:
1031	        """Public fork descriptor S: tip_hash, height, length, status."""
1032	        tip = blocks[-1]
1033	        return {
1034	            "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
1035	            "height": tip.height,
1036	            # The length counts every block including the genesis block.
1037	            "length": len(blocks),
1038	            "status": tip.status,
1039	        }

1041	    def _winning_fork(self) -> tuple[str, list]:
1042	        """Pick the winner among the canonical chain and every candidate.
1043	
1044	        Longest chain wins; equal lengths are broken by the smallest tip hash
1045	        (lexicographic hex order). Returns (tip_hash, block list).
1046	        """
1047	        contenders: list[tuple[str, list]] = [
1048	            (self.store.tip_hash(), self.store.chain)
1049	        ]
1050	        contenders.extend(self.store.forks.items())
1051	        contenders.sort(key=lambda item: (-len(item[1]), item[0]))
1052	        return contenders[0]

1054	    def submit_fork_candidate(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
1055	        """POST /v1/forks/candidates — validate and store a candidate fork.
1056	
1057	        Returns 201 with the fork descriptor S. Malformed or invalid forks
1058	        return 400; a fork already known (identical to the canonical tip or an
1059	        existing candidate tip) returns 409.
1060	        """
1061	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
1062	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
1063	        blocks_raw = payload.get("blocks")
1064	        if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list):
1065	            return 400, {"error": "missing field: blocks (must be a list)"}
1066	        try:
1067	            fork = self.store.validate_fork_blocks(blocks_raw)
1068	        except ValueError as exc:
1069	            return 400, {"error": str(exc)}
1070	        summary = self._fork_summary(fork)
1071	        # An exported fork (the five-field {tip_hash, height, length, status,
1072	        # blocks} document) may be resubmitted verbatim; every supplied summary
1073	        # field is re-verified against the recomputed descriptor.
1074	        for field in ("tip_hash", "height", "length", "status"):
1075	            if field in payload and payload[field] != summary[field]:
1076	                return 400, {"error": f"summary field {field!r} does not match the blocks"}
1077	        tip_hash = fork[-1].block_hash
1078	        with self.store.lock:
1079	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
1080	            # A tip hash equal to any canonical block hash means the candidate
1081	            # is exactly the canonical chain or a prefix of it (the block hash
1082	            # binds height, parent and Merkle root), so it carries nothing new.
1083	            if any(tip_hash == block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain):
1084	                return 409, {"error": "fork is identical to the canonical chain"}
1085	            if tip_hash in self.store.forks:
1086	                return 409, {"error": "candidate fork already exists", "tip_hash": tip_hash}
1087	            self.store.forks[tip_hash] = fork
1088	            try:
1089	                self.store.save()
1090	            except BaseException:
1091	                self.store.forks.pop(tip_hash, None)
1092	                raise
1093	        return 201, self._fork_summary(fork)

1095	    def get_chain(self) -> tuple[int, dict]:
1096	        """GET /v1/chain — canonical chain, candidates sorted by tip hash and
1097	        the adoptable winner (a non-canonical chain that beats canonical).
1098	        """
1099	        with self.store.lock:
1100	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
1101	            canonical = self._fork_summary(self.store.chain)
1102	            candidates = [
1103	                self._fork_summary(self.store.forks[tip])
1104	                for tip in sorted(self.store.forks)
1105	            ]
1106	            winner_tip, winner_chain = self._winning_fork()
1107	            adoptable: list[dict] = []
1108	            if winner_tip != self.store.tip_hash():
1109	                adoptable.append(self._fork_summary(winner_chain))
1110	            return 200, {
1111	                "canonical": canonical,
1112	                "candidates": candidates,
1113	                "adoptable": adoptable,
1114	            }

1116	    def adopt_fork(self, tip_hash: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
1117	        """POST /v1/forks/{tip_hash}/adopt — atomically switch to the winner.
1118	
1119	        Unknown tips return 404; adopting anything other than the current
1120	        winning (longest / smallest-tip-hash) chain returns 409. Adoption
1121	        replaces the canonical chain and mempool in one atomic write that
1122	        advances the generation and rebuilds all indexes; transactions unique
1123	        to the old chain's confirmed history return to the mempool, while
1124	        pending-block transactions never enter it.
1125	        """
1126	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tip_hash):
1127	            return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
1128	        with self.store.lock:
1129	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
1130	            fork = self.store.forks.get(tip_hash)
1131	            if fork is None:
1132	                return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
1133	            winner_tip, _ = self._winning_fork()
1134	            if winner_tip != tip_hash:
1135	                return 409, {"error": "only the winning fork can be adopted"}
1136	            old_chain = self.store.chain
